title: REFERENCE Richards Convergence-Cliff Owner Audit

trigger.characterization: Diagnostic REFERENCE perturbations show a deterministic binary transition from accepted low cost to full-trial Newton exhaustion and transaction retry failure, with no accepted intermediate-cost route.

lineage_reconciliation.reason: F-SI16 owns the newest qualified modifications to the same HeadCalc/legacy-binding files implicated by the F-PE03 cliff. F-SI17 only added a separate process-facing hydraulic-view module.

source_audit_findings_before_start.fsi16_fsi17_nonconvergence_semantics: Newton-loop exhaustion still sets fldecdt, request_dt_reduction and increments internal_retries before returning.
source_audit_findings_before_start.solver_binding_semantics: request_dt_reduction maps to SW_SOLVE_RETRY_ADVISED; the serialized transaction model therefore returns solver_ok=false.
source_audit_findings_before_start.transaction_semantics: A full-trial solver rejection enters the retry ladder before the two-half branch, mass acceptance gate or temporal acceptance gate.

questions: Does the F-PE03 binary convergence cliff reproduce on the exact F-SI16 qualified solver lineage?
Which exact convergence flag or criterion remains active at Newton-loop exhaustion on the first rejected full trial?
Is the transition caused by the legacy convergence contract itself, the explicit numerical controls, or an implementation defect?
Does the same qualitative transition occur for both positive and negative small top-flux perturbations without changing physical configuration?
Can diagnostics expose the deciding convergence criterion without adding persistent per-column state or changing solver semantics?
allowed_initial_work: Test-only reproduction harness on the F-SI16 qualified postimage
Worker-local or test-only diagnostics sufficient to identify the convergence criterion
production_change_gate: Only after exact F-SI16-lineage reproduction and a source-bound diagnosis showing that a production solver change is justified independently of F-PE benchmark needs.
